title: RainbowCake: Mitigating Cold-starts in Serverless with Layer-wise Container Caching and Sharing
problem: Serverless computing suffers from severe cold-start latency when initializing containers. Existing approaches—full container caching, partial container caching, and container sharing—each have significant drawbacks in balancing cold-start mitigation against memory efficiency and burstiness handling.
motivation: Cold-start latency is a critical performance bottleneck that limits the practical adoption and efficiency of serverless computing as a cloud paradigm.
method: RainbowCake caches individual layers of Docker container images—the stacked building blocks that make up a complete image—rather than storing entire containers. When a function starts, it can reuse these cached layers instead of rebuilding from scratch, speeding up startup time. Multiple functions can also share the same running container, reducing wasted memory from underutilized containers.
key_novelty: RainbowCake combines layer-wise container caching with container sharing to achieve both the cold-start speed of traditional full caching and the memory efficiency of standalone sharing.
contributions: Layer-wise container caching mechanism for serverless cold-start mitigation
Container sharing strategy optimized to reduce memory waste while maintaining performance
Combined approach balancing cold-start latency reduction with memory efficiency
Evaluation demonstrating improvements over full/partial caching and container sharing baselines
limitations: Not discussed in the provided abstract.
primary_theme: Serverless cold-start mitigation through layer-wise container caching and sharing
